subject: GPU onboarding matrix & ramp tiers — Helix Health
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: GPU onboarding matrix & ramp tiers — Helix Health

Hi Alicia — great chatting yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together three distinct onboarding paths for dedicated capacity that balance latency SLAs, unit cost, and procurement cadence. Attaching a short one-pager (proposal_helix_dedicated_v1.pdf) and an SLA addendum draft. High-level options: 

1) Pilot lane (low commitment)
   - Minimum guaranteed: 2 A100-equivalent GPUs
   - Peak burst: up to 8 GPUs for 60s bursts
   - Ramp: 30–60 days to full pilot throughput
   - Best if you want to validate integration + evals quickly

2) Production steady state (recommended for initial product launch)
   - Minimum guaranteed: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs
   - Reserved pool: 10 GPUs with autoscale policies to 16 for burst windows
   - Ramp: staged 60/120/180-day increase (2 -> 5 -> 8 guaranteed)
   - SLA targets aligned to SLOs in SLA_addendum_helix.docx

3) High-throughput (for chronic high-QPS workloads)
   - Minimum guaranteed: 24 GPUs, with headroom up to 40 for caching/batching benefits
   - Ramp: multi-quarter onboarding with quarterly capacity reviews

Questions for you so we can lock a recommended path:
- What procurement cadence and approval timeline should we assume (30d, 60d, 90d)?
- Are there any hard constraints around minimum on-prem vs. cloud?
- Which latency percentile (p50/p95) are you targeting for inference?

Next step: if you’re comfortable, we can mark the Production steady state as the recommended option and draft a mutual action plan + DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

Attachments: proposal_helix_dedicated_v1.pdf (pdf, 420KB), SLA_addendum_helix.docx (docx, 58KB)
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@helixhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: GPU onboarding matrix & ramp tiers — Helix Health

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement/approval: target is 60 days, but finance will need a justification for any multi-quarter commitments. We can do pilot within 30 days if pricing is capped.
- Constraint: data residency must stay in our US tenant; on-prem is not an option today.
- Latency target: p95 <= 400ms for text-generation endpoints; embeddings can be higher latency.
- Budget: initial fiscal allocation prefers keeping guaranteed GPUs <= 10 for the first 6 months.

Can you send a 6-month ramp plan that keeps guaranteed GPUs <= 10 but shows economics if we scale to 16? Also need the standard SOC2 attestation and encryption/KMS notes for the private tenancy.

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of AI Platforms, Helix Health
agomez@helixhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-8420

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: GPU onboarding matrix & ramp tiers — Helix Health

Looping in Vivek because finance/ramp cadence impacts commit sizing and our ability to offer tiered discounts. My quick take given Alicia's ask (keep guaranteed <=10 for 6mo):

- Option A (Conservative): 6 guaranteed GPUs, reserved pool 8, burst to 12. Ramp: Month0:2, Month1:4, Month3:6. This keeps their guaranteed baseline under 10 and lets them prove production metrics.
- Option B (Elastic+Savings): 8 guaranteed, reserved pool 10, soft overage to 16 with overage pricing. Ramp faster: Month0:3, Month1:6, Month2:8. Offers better steady throughput and lower p95 due to caching benefits.
- Option C (Staged Commitment with Credits): Start at 4 guaranteed; if they sign a 12-month reservation we tier discounted unit pricing retro to Month1. Ramp: Month0:1, Month1:4, Month4:8.

Notes for proposal: include a migration/runbook for prefix caching and KV warmup to hit p95 targets (we can reduce p95 by ~80ms if we pre-warm top prompts). Also need SOC2 artifact packet + KMS integration checklist for their security team.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GPU onboarding matrix & ramp tiers — Helix Health

Alicia — thanks for the context. Based on your 60-day procurement window and budget cap, we recommend Option A (Conservative) as the initial path with a clear growth trigger to Option B if QoE/throughput justify it. Key points and next steps: 

- Agreed initial configuration (Option A): 6 guaranteed A100-equivalent GPUs, reserved pool configured to 8, automated burst to 12 (burst governed by autoscaler and policy).
- 6-month milestone plan: 
   * Month 0 (provisioning): 2 guaranteed (integration + smoke tests)
   * Month 1 (ramp): scale to 4 guaranteed after infra validation and pilot success metrics
   * Month 3 (stabilize): move to 6 guaranteed and enable production routing
   * Month 6 (review): capacity review for decision to scale toward Option B (8 guaranteed)
- Economics: we modeled unit costs for 6 vs. 8 guaranteed; pivoting to 8 reduces per-token cost ~12% due to batching and cache hit rates. Details in attachment.
- Security/compliance: attaching SOC2 summary and KMS checklist. We will provision within your US tenant and provide signed SLA addendum.
- Paperwork: DocuSign link provided for the initial 6-mo reservation + SLA addendum: https://docusign.com/transaction/3f8b9a2c. I also attached the PDF proposal for procurement.

Action items for Helix: 
- Confirm willingness to commit to the 6-month plan so we can get procurement docs initiated (target sign: within 14 business days)
- Share contact for security review (SOC2 artifact recipient) and a preferred SOW owner for mutual action plan

If you confirm, Ben and I will prepare the signed DocuSign packet and internal activation checklist.

Best,
Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

Attachments: proposal_helix_dedicated_v1.pdf, SLA_addendum_helix.docx
